transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Sofia Nguyen (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM); Ethan Brooks, Maya Ortiz, Ravi Patel, Laura Kim (Silverline Health)

Summary: quick security/compliance review focused on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC/least-privilege for Redwood Private deployment. Customer interested in SCIM provisioning + group mapping, SAML cert rotation, limited admin roles, audit log retention, KMS integration for key management.

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Liam Carter, AE at Redwood, with Sofia our SE and Priya on CS. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Ethan (Head of Security): Doing good, thanks. we've pulled together our identity folks, maya is the IdP lead, ravi handles infra. we want to walk through SAML and SCIM flows and make sure RBAC lines up with our least-privilege profile.
[00:22] Sofia (SE): Great. high level, Redwood supports SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. we also have RBAC at the org and project level - roles like admin, engineer, auditor, and read-only, plus service accounts. we'll show mappings and how just-in-time provisioning and SCIM differ.
[00:40] Maya (Identity Engineer): ok, couple constraints from our end: we use Azure AD as IdP, cert rotation is on a 90-day cadence, we require signed assertions with SHA-256, and we prefer SP-initiated flows for normal SSO. we also need SCIM to provision groups into Redwood with the displayName and externalId preserved.
[01:02] Liam: that makes sense. we support SHA-256 signed assertions; cert rotation is fine - we recommend a short overlap window to avoid login breaks. SP-initiated is fully supported, and IdP-initiated also works but mapping differs slightly.
[01:20] Ravi (Infra Lead): about service accounts and automation: we need programmatic service accounts for our ingestion pipelines but want to ensure they can't access billing or admin actions. how do you handle service account RBAC?
[01:34] Sofia: service accounts are first-class principals. they get explicit role bindings. by default they get 'service' scope but you can restrict to 'infer' only or 'embed' only. we can show a sample policy later; short answer - least-privilege is enforced through role bindings and token scopes, and we have audit logs for actions.
[01:50] Laura (PM): audit logs - retention and export options? we have compliance requirements to keep logs for 2 years and deliver to our SIEM.
[02:00] Priya (CSM): Redwood offers configurable audit log retention for Private customers and you can forward logs to your S3 or to our syslog/forwarder. we also support push to customer-managed SIEM via secure delivery.
[02:16] Ethan: encryption and KMS - we require customer-managed keys for data-at-rest. can Redwood integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[02:25] Liam: yes, for Private deployments we support customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or self-managed HSM). we store only wrapped keys in the control plane; data keys live in the customer environment for private deployments. for hosted we offer Redwood-managed keys but enterprise customers can request bring-your-own-key.
[02:45] Maya: SCIM specifics - can you map groups to Redwood roles? we want group A => engineers, group B => auditors, etc. also is delta provisioning supported (patch) or only full sync?
[02:58] Sofia: we support group-to-role mappings; our SCIM implementation supports PATCH (delta) updates as well as full sync. we also expose an attribute mapping UI and a SaaS endpoint for provisioning. token rotation for SCIM bearer tokens is recommended; we can rotate tokens on our side if you want.
[03:18] Ethan: what about account lifecycle and JIT? we prefer SCIM for controlled provisioning but want JIT as fallback for contractors. any best practice?
[03:28] Sofia: common pattern - use SCIM for full employee provisioning and group sync; enable JIT for external contractors with short-lived guest roles. SCIM gives better lifecycle control and deprovisioning.
[03:40] Liam: let's talk RBAC granularity. you mentioned least-privilege - what operations are sensitive? in Redwood we treat model config changes, billing, and audit log access as higher-privilege. normal inference/invoke is distinct.
[03:54] Maya: we want auditors to have read-only access to logs and usage, engineers to have model-deploy permissions in staging but not production, and ops to control scaling and capacity. can roles be namespace/project-scoped?
[04:08] Sofia: yes - RBAC is hierarchical: org-level admins, project-level roles, and resource tags. you can scope deploy permission to specific projects/environments. we also support custom roles if needed.
[04:24] Ravi: encryption key rotation cadence - if we rotate keys monthly, how do you handle rewrapping? is there downtime?
[04:33] Liam: key rotation is typically seamless - we rewrap data keys and keep old wrapped keys until rewrapping is complete. for Private deployments we do this in-region with no customer-visible downtime; but we schedule rotations during low-traffic windows.
[04:50] Ethan: auditability - do you provide tamper-evident logs or signed audit trails? for SOC 2 we need evidence of immutable logs.
[04:59] Priya: we provide append-only audit logs with tamper-evidence; for Private customers you can forward logs to your immutable storage. our SOC 2 Type II report covers log integrity controls - we'll share the report after the call.
[05:15] Laura: SCIM attribute mapping - is email the primary identifier or can we use externalId? sometimes email changes for people.
[05:23] Sofia: externalId is supported and recommended if emails are mutable. we allow configuring the primary identifier in the SCIM settings.
[05:32] Maya: SAML assertion claims - we need group claims in the assertion for IdP-initiated flows; do you accept group arrays?
[05:40] Liam: yes, we accept group arrays in the assertion, and we also parse group membership via SCIM for canonical mapping. there might be size considerations for very large groups where SCIM is a better option.
[05:55] Ethan: certificate expiry handling - what happens if IdP cert expires unexpectedly?
[06:01] Sofia: we recommend a 2-week overlap on certificate uploads; Redwood accepts multiple certificates per SAML config for smooth rotation. if a cert expires and no overlap exists, users will see SSO failures until rotated. we can add monitoring alerts to your team.
[06:18] Ravi: about session timeouts and SSO session length - can we set short session TTLs for high-risk roles?
[06:25] Liam: yes, session TTLs are configurable per role; high-privilege roles can be configured with stricter timeouts and MFA enforcement.
[06:36] Maya: SCIM rate limits - our identity provider expects us to be conservative; what's your SCIM rate limit?
[06:42] Sofia: default SCIM rate limits are documented; for Private customers we can adjust limits during onboarding. typical rate limit is 10 req/s but we can bump for initial syncs.
[06:55] Ethan: what about delegated admin and RBAC for third-party contractors? we need temp elevated rights with automatic expiry.
[07:03] Sofia: we support temporary role grants and time-bound role bindings; can be integrated with your identity provider or managed in Redwood. auto-expiry is supported and audit logs capture grant/revoke.
[07:16] Laura: any known gaps or limitations we should be aware of?
[07:20] Liam: main limitations are around very large orgs with >100k users - SCIM sync at that scale needs tuning and possibly a dedicated ingestion window. also for hosted customers who require BYOK HSM per-tenant, there are additional setup steps.
[07:34] Ethan: data residency - we need to ensure logs and inference payloads remain in region EU-West. how do you enforce region pinning?
[07:42] Liam: for Private deployments you can pin runtime and storage to region; for Dedicated we support region-aware routing and data residency controls. we'll capture region requirements in the SOW.
[07:55] Maya: can you show a quick example mapping for group->role?
[07:58] Sofia: sure - example we use in docs: SCIM group 'sl-engineers' => Redwood role 'project-engineer' scoped to project 'api-ingest'; SCIM group 'sl-auditors' => Redwood role 'org-auditor' read-only. (link to docs shared in chat)
[08:18] Liam: we'll share the mapping template after call - it's a simple CSV mapping or we can pre-seed during onboarding.
[08:26] Ethan: last question: access to audit logs for our internal auditors - do they need Redwood accounts or can we push logs to their bucket?
[08:35] Priya: both are possible. you can create read-only auditor accounts with constrained RBAC or we can export logs to your S3/GCS for auditor access.
[08:46] Maya: MFA requirements - we enforce MFA via the IdP, but do you have any Redwood-enforced MFA for backups?
[08:53] Sofia: primary MFA enforcement is via IdP. Redwood supports optional enforcement for local accounts, but best practice is IdP-enforced MFA for single sign on.
[09:05] Laura: timeline - we are aiming to start a pilot in Jan, full rollout in Q1. any blockers?
[09:13] Liam: nothing major from our side; we'll send the docs and mapping templates and set up the engineering deep dive.
[09:21] Ethan: thanks, appreciate it.
[09:24] Liam: quick recap of action items and next steps - we'll send SAML metadata, SCIM schema, RBAC examples, SOC 2 docs; customer will confirm IdP rotation windows and provide group naming conventions. schedule deep dive for week of 12/28.
[09:40] End of call.
